climate.overview_html: The defining new development on September 7 is the UNEP Limiting Overshoot report (released September 2), which formally concludes that 1.5°C of warming is now inevitable — the planet will cross that threshold, likely peaking at 1.6–1.8°C, before large-scale carbon dioxide removal can bring it back down. Against that systemic backdrop the active hazard roster remains unchanged: the Nepal–Tibet GLOF holds at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing with no material new toll overnight; the WMO Super El Niño “off the charts” warning from September 3 continues to set the thermodynamic baseline for every active storm in this digest; and EFFIS confirms 647,579 hectares burned across Europe with very extreme fire danger persisting through September 9.

items.headline: UNEP Limiting Overshoot Report: 1.5°C Crossing Now Inevitable; Overshoot Likely to Peak at 1.6–1.8°C; Gigatonne-Scale Carbon Dioxide Removal Required to Descend; Every Tenth of a Degree of Peak Warming Still Matters
items.summary: UNEP's September 2 report formally declares that holding global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels is no longer achievable — the world will cross that threshold and is likely to reach a peak of 1.6–1.8°C before large-scale carbon dioxide removal can bring it back down. The report defines 'overshoot' as the period during which global temperature exceeds 1.5°C, and quantifies the consequences: each additional tenth of a degree significantly increases the probability of crossing irreversible tipping points in the Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, the Amazon rainforest, and Atlantic ocean circulation. UNEP argues that even though 1.5°C is now technically overshot, deep immediate emissions cuts still minimise the height of the overshoot, limit the duration above 1.5°C, and reduce reliance on speculative gigaton-scale CDR to return below threshold. The report arrives as the Super El Niño of 2026 is already driving temperatures to anomalous new highs.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: STABLE — 1,318+ Dead (1,287 Nepal + 31 Tibet); 5,614+ Missing; Debris 240 km Inside India; Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; 5,000+ Rescuers Active
items.summary: No material change in casualty figures reported on September 7: 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet — a combined minimum of 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing. The disaster originated on August 27 from the collapse of a section of Langtang Lirung glacier at approximately 5,200 metres, generating a seismic signal of magnitude Ms 5.2. Debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn surrounding glaciers may still collapse. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations. The event represents one of the deadliest glacial lake outburst floods on instrumental record globally.

items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Near-100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February 2027; 2027 on Track for Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades.' WMO assigned nearly 100% probability that El Niño will persist through at least February 2027. Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 record on the multi-variate ENSO index. Because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, peak atmospheric warming will arrive in 2027, raising the prospect of 2027 becoming the warmest year on record.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 647,579 Hectares Burned (EFFIS Updated September 4) — Very Extreme Fire Danger Through September 9 Across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, Ukraine; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area of 647,579 hectares as of the September 4 data update. Very extreme fire danger is forecast through September 9 across a broad arc from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The 2026 season continues tracking ahead of the long-term average of 328,010 ha for the same date period (2006–2025), though below the record 2025 season tally. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Weakened to Category 3 (115 mph); Hurricane Watch Now Covers Kauaʻi County & Niihau (Upgraded From Tropical Storm Watch); Center ~50 mi SSW of Līhuʻe Sunday PM; Direct Approach; Landfall or Very Close Pass Tonight
major_events.status: CATEGORY 3 · 115 MPH · HW KAUAI COUNTY & NIIHAU · ~50 MI SSW LIHUE SUNDAY PM · LANDFALL TONIGHT
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell has continued weakening from Category 4 (130 mph, Saturday) to Category 3 with maximum sustained winds near 115 mph, but is now in immediate proximity to the Hawaiian Islands: as of Sunday afternoon the center was located approximately 50 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe, Kauaʻi. The Tropical Storm Watch issued Saturday for Kauaʻi County has been upgraded to a Hurricane Watch for Kauaʻi County including Niihau, reflecting the now-imminent threat. The storm made its northward turn as forecast and is tracking directly toward Kauaʻi, expected to make landfall or a very close pass Sunday night or early Monday. Hurricane conditions — sustained winds of 74 mph or higher — are expected on Kauaʻi within hours. Emergency shelters are open across the island; Kauaʻi Civil Defense has urged immediate shelter-in-place. Rainfall totals of 8–15 inches are expected on Kauaʻi with isolated mountain amounts exceeding 20 inches. Storm surge of 2–4 feet above normally dry ground is expected along north and west-facing shores. All flights into Lihue Airport (LIH) are cancelled through Monday morning.

major_events.status: 1,318+ DEAD · 5,614+ MISSING · BARRIER LAKE RISK · RESCUE ONGOING · NO MATERIAL TOLL CHANGE

Chinese authorities continue to warn that surrounding glaciers may still collapse. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police continue search operations.

major_events.status: SERIAN EMERGENCY ONGOING · ~300K HA ACTIVE FIRES · 1.4M STUDENTS REMOTE · CLOUD-SEEDING CONTINUING

major_events.status: ONGOING · 299+ DEAD · PEAK MONSOON · 2–3 MORE SEPTEMBER SPELLS FORECAST

major_events.status: HELD · ~25,163 HA · PHASED RE-ENTRY · SUMMERLAND PARTIAL ORDERS

weather.overview_html: The dominant story on September 7 is Hurricane Lowell’s now-imminent direct threat to Kauaʻi: the storm has weakened to Category 3 (115 mph) but its center is approximately 50 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe as of Sunday afternoon, and the Tropical Storm Watch issued Saturday has been upgraded to a Hurricane Watch for Kauaʻi County and Niihau — with landfall or a very close pass expected Sunday night or early Monday. The remaining board is unchanged: Nepal–Tibet GLOF holds at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing; SE Asia haze affects 1.4 million remote students with ~300,000 ha of active Kalimantan fire; and Europe’s wildfire emergency continues at 647,579 ha with very extreme fire danger through September 9.

items.summary: Hurricane Lowell has continued weakening from Category 4 (130 mph, Saturday) to Category 3 with maximum sustained winds near 115 mph as of Sunday afternoon. However, the storm has completed its northward turn and its center is now approximately 50 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe, Kauaʻi — directly threatening the island. The Tropical Storm Watch issued Saturday for Kauaʻi County and Niihau has been upgraded to a Hurricane Watch, reflecting the now-imminent threat of hurricane-force winds (74+ mph). Kauaʻi Civil Defense has ordered immediate shelter-in-place. Emergency shelters are open across the island. All commercial flights into Lihue Airport (LIH) are cancelled through Monday morning. Forecast precipitation for Kauaʻi: 8–15 inches with isolated mountain totals exceeding 20 inches, sufficient to trigger flash flooding and mudslides in steep terrain. Storm surge of 2–4 feet above normally dry ground is expected along north and west-facing shores. Hurricane conditions are expected to arrive on Kauaʻi by late Sunday evening or Sunday night.

No material change in figures was reported September 7. Flood debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities maintain warnings that surrounding glaciers may still collapse. The event represents one of the deadliest glacial lake outburst floods on instrumental record globally. renewables.overview_html: Three new clean energy project financings from September 1 reshape this week’s renewables picture. Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Gawara Baya Energy announced AUD 1.7 billion financing for a 408 MW wind farm and 104 MW / 416 MWh BESS in Queensland — Australia’s largest announced wind+storage development; ENGIE Chile reached financial close on a 251 MW / 1,004 MWh standalone BESS for USD 384 million, the country’s largest single battery storage contract; and Return Energi and Vattenfall closed the Sirius BESS (200 MW / 800 MWh) in the Netherlands for €180 million, one of Europe’s largest standalone storage projects. The upstream installation milestone from September 1 also holds: OranjeWind (795 MW, RWE/TotalEnergies, Hollandse Kust West VII) completed its first monopile installation using Vestas V236-15 MW turbines, with commercial operations targeted for early 2028.

items.headline: CIP and Gawara Baya Energy: AUD 1.7 Billion Queensland Wind + BESS — 408 MW Wind Farm and 104 MW / 416 MWh Battery; Australia’s Largest Announced Wind+Storage Development; Financial Close Q3 2026; Commercial Operations 2028
items.summary: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Gawara Baya Energy announced the financial close of an AUD 1.7 billion (approximately USD 1.1 billion) wind-plus-battery storage project in Queensland, Australia on September 1 — the largest announced wind and storage co-located development in Australia. The project comprises a 408 MW onshore wind farm co-located with a 104 MW / 416 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). Power purchase agreements cover a portion of output; the remainder sells into the Queensland National Electricity Market. Queensland's energy transition target requires 80% renewables by 2035. Construction is targeted to commence in late 2026 with commercial operations by 2028.

items.headline: ENGIE Chile Financial Close: 251 MW / 1,004 MWh Standalone BESS for USD 384 Million — Chile’s Largest Single Battery Storage Contract; Grid Stabilization on Atacama Solar-Heavy Grid; Operations 2027
items.summary: ENGIE Chile reached financial close on September 1 on a 251 MW / 1,004 MWh standalone battery energy storage system project for USD 384 million — Chile's largest single BESS contract. The system is designed to provide grid stabilization, frequency regulation, and energy shifting on Chile's Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (SEN), which is heavily weighted toward variable solar generation from the Atacama Desert. The project addresses the SEN's growing challenge of managing midday solar surpluses and evening ramping demand — a problem that has caused negative prices in peak solar hours. Commercial operations are expected in 2027.

items.headline: Return Energi and Vattenfall Financial Close: Sirius BESS Netherlands — 200 MW / 800 MWh; €180 Million; One of Europe’s Largest Standalone Storage Projects; Capacity Market Revenue Stack; Operations 2027
items.summary: Return Energi and Vattenfall announced financial close of the Sirius battery energy storage project in the Netherlands on September 1 — a 200 MW / 800 MWh (4-hour duration) system for €180 million, one of Europe's largest standalone battery storage projects. The project is supported by Dutch capacity market revenues and ancillary services contracts. The Netherlands' interconnected position in the European power grid makes large-scale storage valuable for balancing cross-border flows as Dutch and German offshore wind build-out accelerates. Commercial operations are expected in 2027.

items.headline: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) First Monopile Installed — 795 MW RWE/TotalEnergies JV; 53 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbines; 53 km Off Dutch Coast; 1 Million Dutch Households by 2028; Transition-Piece-Less Design
items.summary: The offshore installation vessel Les Alizés successfully installed the first of 53 monopiles for OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) on September 1, 53 km west of IJmuiden in the Dutch North Sea. The 795 MW project is a joint venture between RWE and TotalEnergies, using 53 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines. The project uses innovative transition-piece-less monopiles, where turbine towers bolt directly to the monopile without a transition piece, reducing steel per foundation. Installation of all 53 monopiles is expected to complete by early 2027; turbine installation in 2027; fully operational by early 2028, supplying approximately 1 million Dutch households.

science.overview_html: A new ML paper enters the digest this week: arXiv:2609.03763 (CloudCast v2) extends cloud cover AI forecasting from 1–3 h nowcasting to 12 h lead time at 15-minute temporal and 4-km spatial resolution, achieving a 10% MAE reduction over CloudCast v1 and a 43% bias reduction over the Scandinavian test domain. The headline model release of the period remains Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 — first global AI model on raw observations and live geostationary satellite data, 5-km hourly surface resolution, topping Brightband WeatherBench, live in Google Search/Gemini/Maps. The TC forecasting frontier is directly relevant to Hurricane Lowell’s Sunday-night approach to Kauaʻi: TC-Next (2609.02085) cuts track error 15–44% and intensity error 3–6× vs. conventional trackers with zero-shot transfer across AI and NWP model families, and IMERG fine-tuning (2609.03210) achieves up to 19% CRPS improvement and a 57% Brier skill score gain for extreme rainfall over NWP.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 5-km Global AI Weather Model Trains on Raw Observations; 60% Better Precipitation vs. WN2; 100-m Wind-Height Forecasts; Tops Brightband WeatherBench; Live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based AI models and shrinking it to 3–4 hours with hourly forecast cycles. Resolution: 5 km for key surface variables, 10 km for other surface variables, 25 km for atmospheric variables, and explicit 100-meter hub-height wind forecasts for wind turbine applications alongside cloud cover and solar radiation for grid operators. WeatherNext 3 has 2.4× more parameters than WeatherNext 2. Precipitation evaluation shows CRPS improvements of up to 60% against IMERG and 50% Brier score reduction versus NWP baselines at early lead times. On Brightband's Operational WeatherBench, WeatherNext 3 ranks first across temperature, wind speed, and humidity. Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Google Earth Engine.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecast — GloSea6 Underestimates TC Frequency, Tracks, Lifetime, and Intensity; Largest Errors in August; Downscaling Partially Corrects Bias
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates the characteristics of tropical cyclones in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6, the operational seasonal-to-sub-seasonal forecasting model of the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), over the western North Pacific during JJAS 1993–2016. GloSea6 is found to underestimate TC frequency, tracks (particularly in mid-latitudes), lifetime, and intensity across all months, with the most significant errors occurring in August. The paper evaluates whether dynamical downscaling to higher resolution can recover the lost skill for track and intensity. The results are directly relevant to the current Super El Niño season, during which TC forecast accuracy is critical for Hawaii (Lowell), the Philippines, and Japan.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210: Fine-Tuning AI Weather Model With IMERG Precipitation Observations Improves Medium-Range CRPS by Up to 19% and Extreme Rainfall Brier Skill by 57%; Tropical Storms and Drizzle Also Improved
items.meta: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain · arXiv:2609.03210 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: Artificial intelligence weather prediction (AIWP) systems now surpass state-of-the-art physical models for medium-range forecasting, but current global AIWP models are trained almost exclusively on the ERA5 reanalysis, which has known biases particularly for precipitation. This paper fine-tunes a graph-transformer AIWP architecture directly with IMERG precipitation observational data at 0.25° resolution. Results: medium-range CRPS improves by up to 19%; Brier skill score for extreme rainfall prediction improves by 57% globally over state-of-the-art operational NWP models. The fine-tuned model also demonstrates superior skill for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events. The approach is directly relevant to the acute precipitation hazards active in this digest: Hurricane Lowell threatening Hawaii, Pakistan's monsoon, and Nepal's ongoing flood response.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.02085 (TC-Next): Zero-Shot Multimodal Cyclone Forecasting — Trained Only on GraphCast/Western Pacific; Cuts Track Error 15–44% and Intensity Error 3–6× vs. Conventional Trackers; Transfers Without Retraining to Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES
items.meta: Wang, Chen, Luo, Kim, Chang · arXiv:2609.02085 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: TC-Next is a multimodal deep learning model that forecasts tropical cyclone track and intensity at 6–24 h lead times by jointly leveraging a foundation model's atmospheric forecast fields (kinematic and thermodynamic) and GridSat infrared satellite imagery. Trained exclusively on GraphCast forecast fields over the Western Pacific, TC-Next lowers track error by 15–44% and intensity error by a factor of 3–6 relative to the conventional rule-based tracker TempestExtremes. Critically, when applied zero-shot — without retraining — to forecast fields from Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES, TC-Next remains substantially ahead of TempestExtremes on both track and intensity, demonstrating strong model-agnostic generalization.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Winner MicroEnsemble (Microsoft-Led) Post-Processes ECMWF Dynamics With AI; Annual Awards Ceremony September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition phase: August 2025–September 2026 · Annual awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international competition for AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting operating from August 2025 to September 2026 — is concluding its first year, with an annual highlights and awards ceremony scheduled for September 24. Forty-two teams from 30+ countries submitted real-time global sub-seasonal forecasts at 1.5° resolution, providing quintile probabilities for weekly-mean temperature, precipitation, and sea level pressure for the Days 19–25 and Days 26–32 windows. The DJF 2025/26 period winner was MicroEnsemble, a Microsoft-led team whose approach uses AI to post-process state-of-the-art dynamical ECMWF forecasts — a hybrid AI-physical approach. ECMWF's own AIFS-SUBS submission extended skilful MJO forecasts by 8 days using approximately 200× less energy at inference than the dynamical model.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud Cover Forecasting Extended From 1–3 h to 12 h Lead Time; 10% MAE Reduction Over CloudCast v1; 43% Bias Reduction; 15-Minute Temporal and 4-km Spatial Resolution Over Scandinavia
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends the original CloudCast machine learning nowcasting system — which forecasted cloud cover at 1–3 hour lead times — to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution. The model is trained and evaluated over Scandinavia using MSG satellite data. Key results: 10% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) versus CloudCast v1; 43% reduction in systematic bias in the Scandinavian domain; improved skill at extended 6–12 h lead times where the original system degraded most sharply. Longer cloud cover forecasts have direct applications for solar power ramp forecasting, aviation, and solar resource assessment — important as Northern European grids integrate increasing shares of variable PV generation.

items.source: arXiv / Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD 2026
items.headline: arXiv 2609.00847: First Comprehensive Checklist for Energy and Carbon Footprints of ML/AI in Earth System Modeling; Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Presented at GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026 Naples
items.meta: Dainelli, Mozaffari, Castaño et al. (BSC Earth Dept.) · arXiv:2609.00847 · September 1, 2026 · GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026, Naples
items.summary: As machine learning finds its way into nearly every aspect of Earth system modeling, this Barcelona Supercomputing Center paper provides the first comprehensive checklist for ML/AI practitioners to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their applications. The checklist is organized around successive pipeline stages — data curation, model architecture, training regime, inference, and deployment — with curated metrics for estimating energy consumption and carbon footprint at each stage. The work is timely given the explosive growth of compute-intensive neural weather models such as WeatherNext 3, GraphCast, and AIFS. Presented at the GREEN-AI workshop of ECML PKDD 2026 in Naples.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end AI weather system probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder capturing aleatoric uncertainty; (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor capturing epistemic uncertainty. A law-of-total-variance decomposition attributes forecast spread to each source. Key result: probabilistic fine-tuning improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension.

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — Dedicated ILS, Structured Reinsurance, and Capital Markets Unit; Responds to Record $171B Verisk AAL Benchmark and Growing Alternative Capacity Demand
items.body_html: Howden Re launched its International Alternative Solutions (IAS) practice on September 6, a dedicated unit consolidating ILS placement, catastrophe bond issuance, collateralised reinsurance, and structured capital capabilities under a single leadership team. The launch comes as Verisk’s new $171 billion average annual insured loss benchmark reinforces broker and cedant demand for alternative capacity beyond traditional reinsurance limits. Hurricane Lowell’s Sunday-night approach to Kauaʻi provides real-time illustration of the Super El Niño-driven exposure escalation that is reshaping cat reinsurance pricing and structure.

items.title: Swiss Re: Data Centers and AI Workloads Create $200 Billion Premium Opportunity for Property Insurers; Renewables Integration Compounds Risk Complexity; Presented at Monte Carlo Rendez-vous
items.body_html: Swiss Re released a research report at the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous on September 5 calculating that data centers and AI workloads represent a USD 200 billion global premium opportunity for property and casualty insurers over the next decade, driven by capital expenditure growth in hyperscaler infrastructure, increasingly dense equipment values, and emerging AI-driven operational exposures. The report identifies three layers of compounding risk: physical climate risk to data center locations (flood, wildfire, extreme heat affecting cooling systems); grid reliability risk as renewables integration creates frequency and voltage events; and cyber-physical risk from AI model failure cascades. Swiss Re argues that the insurance industry needs parametric and structured capacity mechanisms to underwrite these risks at scale, and that traditional property per-occurrence limits are structurally insufficient for large hyperscaler campuses.

items.title: Cummins Joins Emerald Technology Ventures as Limited Partner — Industrial Decarbonization Focus; Emerald Fund VII Targets Energy Transition and Industrial Efficiency
items.body_html: Cummins Inc., the global power technology manufacturer, joined Emerald Technology Ventures’ Fund VII as a limited partner on September 1, focusing on industrial decarbonization. Emerald Technology Ventures is a specialist deep-tech climate venture firm based in Zurich and San Francisco with a 25-year track record in industrial energy efficiency and clean energy. Fund VII targets early-to-growth-stage companies in energy transition, industrial efficiency, and advanced materials — themes directly aligned with Cummins’ Destination Zero strategy to eliminate carbon from its engines and power systems.

items.title: Cyclic Materials Closes $75 Million Series C Led by T. Rowe Price to Scale US Rare Earth Recycling — Total Equity Now $237 Million; Arizona Facility Operational Q3 2026; South Carolina Campus Breaking Ground Q4; Critical Supply for Wind Turbines and EV Magnets
items.body_html: Cyclic Materials, a Canadian rare earth recycling company, closed a $75 million Series C financing round announced September 2, 2026, led by accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, bringing total equity funding to $237 million. Strategic investor ERI joined the round alongside existing backers Microsoft, Amazon, and others. Cyclic’s Hub-and-Spoke system recovers rare earth materials from permanent magnets in end-of-life wind turbines, EV motors, and manufacturing scrap. An Arizona magnet separation and critical mineral recycling plant is expected to begin operations during Q3 2026, with a South Carolina integrated rare earth recycling campus breaking ground in Q4 2026.

items.title: Artemis London 2026: Cat Bond and ILS Market Well-Positioned for Disciplined Growth; AFME Calls for ILS to Back Climate Policies; 220 Attendees, 120+ Organizations
items.body_html: The Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1 convened approximately 220 attendees from more than 120 organizations across the ILS ecosystem. Speakers highlighted discipline in the catastrophe bond market and expected continued growth. The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME) called for ILS and catastrophe bonds as effective mechanisms for insurers to access new capital to back climate-related policies — directly relevant as the Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, released the same day, put average annual insured losses at a record $171 billion.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%); 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from the prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%.
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal
